--- a/task_template.md
+++ b/task_template.md
@@ -58,9 +58,19 @@
   =WORKDAY(...)) recalculates correctly — keep it when the answer must track per-copy data.
   But confirm the value it will RECALCULATE to, not merely that the text was written.
-- These do NOT reliably recalculate headlessly and grade as blank/stale: array/CSE formulas
-  (openpyxl ArrayFormula), dynamic-array functions (UNIQUE/FILTER/SORT), TEXTJOIN, AGGREGATE,
-  and any formula whose inputs are volatile (RAND/RANDBETWEEN/NOW/TODAY, directly or
-  transitively). For these, compute the answer in Python and write the LITERAL result (a real
-  number / str / bool / datetime) instead of the live formula.
+- These answer-cell formula TYPES do NOT reliably recalculate headlessly and grade as
+  blank/stale: array/CSE formulas (openpyxl ArrayFormula), dynamic-array functions
+  (UNIQUE/FILTER/SORT), TEXTJOIN, and AGGREGATE. When YOUR answer cell would itself hold one of
+  these, compute the result in Python and write the LITERAL (a real number / str / bool /
+  datetime) instead of the live formula.
+- But do NOT literalize a formula just because a cell it READS is volatile or formula-driven.
+  If the instruction asks you to PUT or FIX a formula, or the answer must LOOK UP / reference
+  cells that themselves contain volatile functions (RANDBETWEEN/RAND/NOW/TODAY) or other
+  formulas, keep the answer as a LIVE ordinary formula (IF/SUMPRODUCT/COUNTIF/VLOOKUP/
+  INDEX-MATCH). The grader recalculates the whole workbook, so a live formula tracks the
+  regenerated/recalculated source in lockstep with the reference, whereas a Python snapshot of
+  those source cells captures pre-recalc (e.g. old random) values and grades stale. In
+  particular, for a "fix the broken formula" task whose corrected formula is an ordinary
+  recalculable one, write the corrected LIVE formula — a Python-computed bool/int/number in its
+  place can grade as the wrong value or type.
 - A formula that evaluates to "" writes a BLANK cell and lowers coverage — if a cell must be
   filled, make sure your result is a real value, not an empty string.
@@ -89,9 +99,21 @@
   source cell's own value AND python type — do not coerce a number into text or text into a
   number/date, and never leave an unresolved "=..." formula string in an answer cell.
-- When you SPLIT or EXTRACT a piece out of a text cell, keep that piece as the original text
-  (str), preserving its spacing — do not parse the piece into a date or number. This holds even
+- A number produced by an Excel formula or by recalculation is stored as a FLOAT. When a
+  worked-example or reference cell in the target range holds a whole number as a float (e.g.
+  28.0, 66.0 — not a plain int), write your computed answer as a float too: a Python int where
+  the reference holds a float grades as the wrong type. Match the example cell's numeric type
+  whenever one is present in the range on any copy.
+- When you SPLIT or EXTRACT a piece out of a text cell into generic "parts"/"sections" that the
+  instruction does NOT name as a typed value, keep that piece as the original text (str),
+  preserving its spacing — do not parse it into a date or number. This str default holds even
   when a pre-filled example cell in the range already HOLDS a real datetime/number value (not
-  merely a date number_format): for a split/extract, the operation dictates the output type, not
-  the example cell's stored type — every extracted piece stays a str.
+  merely a date number_format), and even when the piece happens to look like a date or number:
+  for such a generic split, the operation dictates str output, not the example cell's stored type.
+- EXCEPTION — when the instruction's OWN request names the extracted result as a date, time,
+  number, id/code, or count (e.g. "extract the dates into column E", "split the ids into
+  columns", "pull out the amount"), produce the REAL typed value: a datetime for a named date, a
+  float/int for a named number/id/count — never its text form. Decide by what the instruction
+  asks you to PRODUCE, NOT by a date/number merely appearing in a column header, in the source
+  text, or in a pre-filled example cell.
 - When the instruction asks you to CONVERT or STANDARDIZE a whole value into a date/time/number
   (e.g. "reformat as dd/mm/yy"), store a real datetime/number and set the cell's number_format
